title: RosettaSearch: Multi-Objective Inference-Time Search for Protein Sequence Design
authors: Meghana Kshirsagar, Allen Nie, Ching-An Cheng, Fanglei Xue, Rahul Dodhia, Juan Lavista Ferres, Kevin K. Yang, Frank DiMaio
code_and_data_released: Promised on GitHub upon release (Sec 7); no repository URL available in preprint.

methods.datasets: ~400 (394 in Table 3 / 414 in Sec 6) low-fidelity PDB-D monomers, 275 de novo RFdiffusion backbones from Dayhoff Atlas (no native sequence context), and 48 (50 sampled) BindCraft binders.
methods.evaluation_protocol: Inference-time Priority Search / Sequential Revision over 75 RosettaFold3 (RF3, single-sequence no-MSA) calls per protein (3 textual step sizes x 25 RF3 calls; ~30.6 min/protein), guided by local residue-range pLDDT/TM-score/RMSD text feedback.
methods.controls_included: Budget-matched random mutations in flagged regions, Dayhoff no-native-sequence test, independent Chai-1 refolding evaluation, and context ablation table (Table 7). Missing: compute-matched LigandMPNN/ProteinMPNN best-of-75 + RF3 selection baseline.
methods.compute_and_tools: 75 RF3 folding evaluations + LLM search (~30.6 min/protein) vs single-pass LigandMPNN/ProteinMPNN.
methods.metrics: Single-sequence pLDDT, TM-score, Ca RMSD, SR-1 (pLDDT >= 0.8 & TM >= 0.8), SR-2 (+ RMSD <= 1.5 A) under RF3 and Chai-1.

key_results.benchmark: 275 Dayhoff de novo backbones (no native sequence context)
key_results.notes: No native sequence leakage on Dayhoff, showing genuine RF3-guided search gains, but lacks a compute-matched ProteinMPNN-75 + RF3 baseline and Chai-1 cross-check on Dayhoff.

key_results.llm_model: RosettaSearch (o4-mini + native sequence in prompt + 75 RF3 calls)
key_results.llm_score: 20.5% (RF3) -> 5.3% (Chai-1); without native seq in prompt: 11.4% RF3 (Table 7)
key_results.baseline_score: 7.9% (RF3) / 3.1% (Chai-1) for both LigandMPNN and Random mutations
key_results.notes: Native sequence in prompt drives much of the PDB gain (11.4% -> 17.2%, Sec 3.2.2 notes LLM returning the native sequence), and RF3 overfitting cuts absolute SR-1 from 20.5% to 5.3% on Chai-1.

temporal_cutoff.evidence: PDB-D monomers and BindCraft binders predate o4-mini and Gemini-3 with no cutoff holdout.

homology_overlap.evidence: Randomly sampled from PDB-D without homology clustering (RF3 runs MSA-free).

cross_modal_literature_recall.evidence: PDB prompts explicitly supply the native sequence (Fig 10), raising SR-1 from 11.4% to 17.2% (Table 7), and Sec 3.2.2 documents the LLM returning the native sequence itself (Dayhoff removes this).

preprocessing_artifacts.evidence: Sec 3.2.2 and A.4-A.5 document proxy hacking (poly-Ala tails, repeats, safe-residue overuse) and 44% (22/50) trace validation failures (budget violations, indexing bugs), plus minor N mismatches (394 vs 414).

downstream_oracle_filtering.evidence: Direct 75-call RF3 reward optimization exhibits heavy RF3 overfitting: PDB SR-1 drops from 20.5% under RF3 to 5.3% under independent Chai-1 (Table 2).

compute_and_tool_asymmetry.evidence: Compares 75 RF3-guided LLM search calls (~30.6 min/protein) against single-pass LigandMPNN/ProteinMPNN.

baseline_fairness.evidence: No budget-matched LigandMPNN/ProteinMPNN best-of-75 + RF3 selection baseline or ResiDPO comparison (only random mutations are budget-matched).

data_and_wetlab_transparency.evidence: Purely in silico (no wet-lab validation) and code/data not yet released.

takeaway: RosettaSearch shows inference-time LLM priority search over RosettaFold3 feedback improves single-pass ProteinMPNN/LigandMPNN sequences (reaching 89.5% vs 72.4% SR-1 on Dayhoff de novo backbones without native sequences) and beats budget-matched random mutations. However, PDB gains lean heavily on placing the native sequence in the prompt, RF3 overfitting drops PDB success from 20.5% to 5.3% on Chai-1, and no budget-matched MPNN best-of-75 baseline or wet-lab check is provided.
